notes: RocksDB (Facebook LSM-tree) via rocksdict, in-process, thread-safe. Same modelling as LMDB (ordered key-value + hand-maintained index keyspaces, WriteBatch for atomic multi-key writes). Write-optimised (LSM) vs LMDB's read-optimised B+tree. No server, no network, no replication.

secondary_index.title: Create a secondary index on a non-key field and use it
secondary_index.detail: no query engine; application-maintained ordered index keyspaces (idx/...)

compound_index.title: Compound / composite index over two fields
compound_index.detail: composite ordered keys built by hand

unique_constraint.title: Unique constraint on a non-key field (duplicate rejected)
unique_constraint.detail: keys are unique; no constraint on values

ttl_expiry.title: Native per-document/key expiry
ttl_expiry.detail: no native TTL (store an expiry field and sweep; RocksDB has a TTL column-family option)

partial_update.title: Update a single field without rewriting the document
partial_update.detail: read-modify-write the whole value (no in-place field update; the value is an opaque blob)

atomic_increment.title: Server-side atomic numeric increment
atomic_increment.detail: read-modify-write under the single-writer lock -> [(363,)] (atomic because one writer at a time)

optimistic_concurrency.title: Compare-and-set / version or ETag-guarded write
optimistic_concurrency.detail: application-level CAS: read value, compare, write in one write txn/batch -> [(1, 2)]

multi_doc_transaction.title: Multi-document / multi-key ACID transaction with rollback
multi_doc_transaction.detail: atomic multi-key write batch (LMDB: one write transaction, fully ACID; RocksDB: WriteBatch, atomic + durable)

tunable_consistency.title: Per-request consistency / write concern / read preference
tunable_consistency.detail: single local writer: reads are always consistent within a transaction snapshot (LMDB MVCC; RocksDB snapshot)

nested_query.title: Filter on a field inside a nested object
nested_query.detail: no implementation for this engine family

array_operators.title: Query and update array-valued fields (contains, push)
array_operators.detail: values are opaque; array handling is in your encoding/decoding

server_side_join.title: Join / lookup between two collections inside the engine

change_streams.title: Change feed / watch / keyspace notifications
change_streams.detail: no change feed (RocksDB has a WAL/EventListener at the C++ level, not exposed here)

server_side_scripting.title: Stored procedures / Lua / JS / UDF executed by the server
server_side_scripting.detail: in-process library: 'server-side' is your own code

pubsub.title: Publish/subscribe messaging built into the engine

explain_plan.title: Query plan / profile output for a query
explain_plan.detail: no planner; access is whatever key/range you request

bulk_import.title: Native bulk import path (bulk API, batch, COPY-like tool)
bulk_import.detail: batched write transaction / WriteBatch (what the load phase uses)

large_document.title: Store and read back a 15 MB document / value
large_document.detail: 15 MB value ok (LMDB single value limit is bounded by map size; RocksDB by memory)

many_fields.title: Document with 5000 top-level fields
many_fields.detail: value is an opaque blob; field count is up to your encoding

read_from_replica.title: Client can direct reads to a replica / secondary
read_from_replica.detail: single local file; replication is external (Litestream-style log shipping)

snapshot_backup.title: Online snapshot / backup command available
snapshot_backup.detail: consistent on-disk copy while open (LMDB: env.copy(compact) / mdb_copy -c; RocksDB: Checkpoint hard links) — exercised in the backup phase

incremental_backup.title: Incremental / differential backup (file- or segment-level)
incremental_backup.detail: LMDB: full copy only; RocksDB BackupEngine does incremental (not exposed by rocksdict, Checkpoint is full via hard links)

pitr.title: Point-in-time recovery from a continuous change log
pitr.detail: no change log to replay (RocksDB WAL is not a PITR log); Litestream-style shipping is external

slow_query_log.title: Server-side slow-query log with a configurable threshold
slow_query_log.detail: no server: time the calls in the application (a decorator around txn/get/scan)

audit_log.title: Audit / full-query log of statements or auth events
audit_log.detail: no server: audit in the application

structured_logs.title: JSON-structured server log out of the box
structured_logs.detail: LMDB has no log; RocksDB writes its info LOG (text) into the DB dir

runtime_log_level.title: Change log verbosity at run time (no restart)
runtime_log_level.detail: RocksDB info_log_level / stats period are open-time options; LMDB has none

get_by_key.title: Point read: customer by primary key

multi_get.title: Batch point read: 100 customers by key in one request

update_field.title: Partial update: set one field of a customer

upsert.title: Upsert inventory row by composite key

atomic_increment.title: Server-side atomic increment of a numeric field

batch_insert_1000.title: Bulk write: 1000 events in one request

range_by_secondary.title: Secondary lookup: orders of one customer

range_by_time.title: Range scan: events of one type in a 3-day window

filter_nested.title: Filter on a nested field + top-level field

top_n_sorted.title: Top-N with sort: 10 most expensive active products of a category

join_lookup.title: Orders of a customer with the customer's name (server-side join if the engine has one)

graph_traversal.title: Category ancestor chain of a product (variable-depth traversal)

geo_near.title: Geo radius query on customer locations

transaction_transfer.title: Multi-document atomic transfer between two inventory rows

opt01_secondary_index.title: Range scan on events(event_type, occurred_at): no index vs secondary index (both column orders)
opt01_secondary_index.what: an access path that is not indexed is a full scan; composite order matters on B-tree-like engines

variants.name: ordered_index_(type,ts,id)
variants.setup: built i/e_type/* ordered index over 1000008 events

opt02_projection.title: Point read of an order: whole document (with embedded items) vs 3-field projection
opt02_projection.what: returning fewer fields saves serialisation and transfer; some engines still read the whole document

opt03_pagination.title: Deep pagination: offset/skip vs keyset (cursor) at depth 10k and 100k
opt03_pagination.what: offset still walks and discards rows; a keyset cursor seeks directly into the sorted index

opt04_batching.title: Write batching: 2000 events one-by-one vs 2 bulk requests of 1000
opt04_batching.what: round trips dominate small writes; every engine has a bulk path (insert_many, pipeline, batch, _bulk)

opt05_multi_get.title: 100 point reads: sequential round trips vs one multi-get request
opt05_multi_get.what: batched reads (MGET / $in / IN / mget / pipelining) amortise the network round trip

opt06_embedding_vs_reference.title: Order with its items: embedded array (one document) vs referenced (order + items lookup)
opt06_embedding_vs_reference.what: embedding what is read together avoids a second query / join; referencing keeps documents small and items independently addressable

opt07_write_durability.title: Single-document write at each durability / write-concern level the engine offers
opt07_write_durability.what: acknowledgement level (replica acks, fsync, refresh) is the biggest lever on write latency

opt08_read_consistency.title: Point read at each read consistency level / read preference the engine offers
opt08_read_consistency.what: linearizable / quorum reads cost extra round trips; replica reads trade freshness for offload

opt09_connection_reuse.title: Point read with a new connection per operation vs one persistent client
opt09_connection_reuse.what: handshakes (TCP, TLS, auth, topology discovery) dwarf a point read; always pool

write_contention.interpretation: every accepted CAS advanced the version exactly once: atomic compare-and-set

loadtest.note: embedded single-process engine: see optimize opt04 batching for write throughput

strategy.tool: Checkpoint.create_checkpoint(dir): hard-links the immutable SSTs + copies MANIFEST/CURRENT/WAL — an openable DB in milliseconds; BackupEngine (C++) adds incremental backups
strategy.restore: offline for the process: close, replace the DB directory with the checkpoint, reopen
strategy.incremental: BackupEngine only (not exposed by rocksdict); checkpoints share SST files through hard links
strategy.pitr: none (the WAL is for crash recovery, not replay to a timestamp)
strategy.schedule: the application (checkpoint on a timer, then rsync/upload the directory)
strategy.retention: delete old checkpoint dirs (SSTs are freed when the last link goes)
